title: Two Dissertations (De morte Christi Cap. 1-6 partial)
author: John Davenant
edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Wing D317; ESTC R5446. IA bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_dissertationes-du-_davenant-john-bp_1650. Partial: De morte Christi Cap. 1 Thesis 1 + Cap. 2 Ratios 1-ultima + Cap. 3 Satisfit through Obj. 17 + Cap. 4 Thesis 2 tip through Mem. 1 close + Cap. 4 Mem. 2 through Mem. 3 tip + Cap. 4 Mem. 3 possible-faith remainder through Thesis 2 close + Cap. 5 Thesis 3 tip through Mem. 2 Scripture close + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Rat. 1-4 (contact/faith-union through acceptance) + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Fathers tip (Ambrose through Bernard close) + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Huberiana objections tip (adversaries opened through Obj. 3 Solut close) + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 elect-from-eternity objections tip (Obj. 1 through Obj. 3 Solut close) + Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Scripture elect objections tip (Proferri etiam through Cap. 5 thesis close) + Cap. 6 opening tip (Thesis ultima through Arg. 1 close) + Cap. 6 Arg. 2 through Arg. 8 Primo close + Cap. 6 Arg. 8 Prosper Resp. 4 / Fulgentius Primo close through Secundo Fathers concord on vivifying grace before Pelagian-mode digression.
blurb: John Davenant — Dissertation on the Death of Christ from the 1650 Cambridge Latin. Covers Cap. 1 controversy-origin, Thesis 1, Cap. 2 Ratios 1 through the ultima ratio, Cap. 3 Satisfit through Obj. 17 (Cap. 3 close), Cap. 4 Thesis 2 tip through first-member close, Cap. 4 Mem. 2 through Mem. 3 tip, Cap. 4 Mem. 3 possible-faith remainder through Thesis 2 close, Cap. 5 Thesis 3 tip through Mem. 2 Scripture close, Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Rat. 1-4, Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Fathers tip, Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Huberiana objections tip, Cap. 5 Mem. 2 elect-from-eternity objections tip, Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Scripture elect objections tip through Cap. 5 close, Cap. 6 opening tip through Arg. 1 close, Cap. 6 Arg. 2 through Arg. 8 Primo, and Cap. 6 Arg. 8 Prosper Resp. 4 / Fulgentius through Secundo Fathers concord on vivifying grace; Cap. 6 Arg. 8 Pelagian-mode remainder through Cap. 11 and De praedestinatione remain.
era_note: Davenant wrote in the early seventeenth century as Lady Margaret Professor at Cambridge and Bishop of Salisbury; he was a British delegate at Dort. This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
